title: Explaining Black-Box Language Models: Learning to Optimize Linguistically-Structured Word Subsets

problem.claim: Understanding the decision rationale of black-box deep language models is important for trust, safety, and accountability, but internal model states are inaccessible.

gap.claim: Existing explanation methods do not concurrently provide inference-time efficiency, black-box compatibility without out-of-distribution behavior, and explanations grounded in linguistic structure.

contributions.claim: A method explains deep language model predictions by selecting a small, informative subset of input words.
The method formulates word-subset selection as an amortized optimization problem for efficient one-shot inference without input-specific search.
A REINFORCE-style policy-gradient selection policy performs discrete word selection in a gradient-free setting and incorporates graph-structured knowledge to produce linguistically coherent subsets.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The method was evaluated on diverse deep language model architectures and multiple real-world datasets.
The method reportedly identified word subsets with enhanced discriminative power and stronger alignment with linguistically salient cues.
The method reportedly outperformed conventional black-box-compatible methods and gradient-based approaches with oracle gradient access on a more challenging benchmark.

narrative_sequence.summary: High-stakes deployment makes understanding language-model decision rationale important.
Black-box access restricts internal states, and existing methods fail to satisfy efficiency, compatibility, and linguistic comprehensibility together.
The proposed approach selects informative word subsets using amortized optimization, gradient-free policy learning, and graph-structured linguistic knowledge.
The method was evaluated across diverse architectures and real-world datasets, with reported gains over several comparison methods.
The authors report that code is available.

source_observation.claim: The method combines amortized selection with linguistic graph structure to generate efficient and linguistically coherent explanations.

interpretation.claim: Explanation quality may benefit from jointly optimizing computational efficiency and alignment with interpretable input structure.

application.claim: For black-box text-model explanations, consider selecting compact input subsets with a learned policy while incorporating domain-relevant linguistic relationships.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported architectures, datasets, or linguistic graph construction.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative results, dataset names, model names, or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not specify the linguistic graph source or construction procedure.
The abstract does not provide limitations, computational costs, or the code URL.
